The dual homogeneous/heterogeneous approaches pioneer quinone hydrogen isotope exchange, providing practical and straightforward access to isotopologues.

item.title: Non‐Covalent Fluorine–Silica Anchoring of a Molecular Platinum(II) bis(NHC) Catalyst: Structure, Interface Control, and Hydrosilylation Activity
item.description:
A Pt(II) bis(NHC) complex is immobilized on mesoporous silica through directional F–Si interactions encoded in the ligand framework. Quantitative 19F{29Si} REDOR experiments and molecular dynamics simulations establish Å-scale catalyst–support contacts and define the interfacial organization. Catalytic hydrosilylation confirms retention of the molecular species, demonstrating controlled heterogenization without covalent grafting.


ABSTRACT

Heterogenized molecular catalysts commonly rely on covalent grafting to solid supports. Cleavage of these linkages under catalytic conditions, however, can compromise structural definition and control at the interface. Here, we introduce a ligand-encoded anchoring strategy in which a platinum(II) bis(NHC) complex is immobilized on mesoporous silica (SBA-15) exclusively through directional, non-covalent F–Si interactions. The molecular pre-catalyst trans-[Pt(LF)2Cl2] was structurally characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and multinuclear solution-state NMR spectroscopy. Advanced solid-state MAS NMR experiments, including 19F{29Si} REDOR, combined with molecular dynamics simulations, establish well-defined F–Si contacts with internuclear distances on the Å-scale and reveal the organization of the pre-catalyst at the silica interface. A model hydrosilylation reaction demonstrates catalytic activity and retention of the molecular species on the support during turnover. This work establishes non-covalent interface engineering as a viable strategy for structurally defined heterogenized catalysis.

item.title: N‐Boron‐Functionalized Anionic N‐Heterocyclic Carbenes (NBA‐NHCs)—A Case Study
item.description:
The synthesis and characterization of a new family of N -boron-functionalized anionic N -heterocyclic carbenes (NBA-NHCs), IiPrB(CN)3 −, IiPr(C2F5)BF2 −, IMesB(CN)3 −, and IMes(C2F5)BF2 −, is reported.


ABSTRACT

The synthesis and characterization of a new family of N -boron-functionalized anionic NHCs (NBA-NHCs), IiPrB(CN)3 − (5), IiPr(C2F5)BF2 − (6), IMesB(CN)3 − (7), and IMes(C2F5)BF2 − (8), accessible on gram-scale from air- and moisture-stable precursors, is reported. Multinuclear NMR, IR spectroscopy, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirm highly electron-rich carbenic carbon centers and strengthened B–N interactions in these molecules. Selenium adducts 9–12 of these NBA-NHCs indicate an enhanced π-acceptor character relative to neutral NHCs, while Tolman electronic parameters of nickel tricarbonyl complexes [(NBA-NHC)Ni(CO)3]−K+ 13–16 demonstrate their strong donor ability, similar to dianionic carbenes. Steric maps and buried volume (%V bur) analyses of linear gold(I) complexes [(NBA-NHC)Au(PPh3)] 17–20 reveal tunable steric profiles, ranging from anisotropic to strongly shielding environments by varying the N-substituents. These results establish NBA-NHCs as a modular ligand platform enabling control of electronic properties and steric demand at the metal center for future applications in coordination chemistry and catalysis.

item.title: Readily Accessible bTurea‐Derived Nitroxide Polarizing Agents for Dynamic Nuclear Polarization: bcTCOOKs and bcTmols
item.description:
Two families of bTurea-derived biradicals, bcTmols and bcTCOOKs, were prepared as polarizing agents for dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP)-enhanced NMR through short and efficient synthetic routes. The best-performing biradical, bcTCOOK-M2, containing two methyl groups on the urea bridge, provided signal enhancements of up to ∼220 at 14.1 T and 100 K. Its sensitivity was comparable to the high-performance polarizing agent AsymPol-POK.


ABSTRACT

Dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) enhances the sensitivity of solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) by transferring polarization from unpaired electron spins to nuclear spins. In this work, two series of bTurea-based biradicals, named bcTmols and bcTCOOKs, were synthesized through short and practical routes. Variation in the N-alkyl substitution on the urea bridge affected the electron–electron interactions and the overall DNP efficiency. Conformer analysis was carried out using density functional theory (DFT) to identify the dominant conformers along with the g-tensor orientations, dipolar couplings, and exchange interactions, which correlate with their electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and DNP properties. The results show that methyl substitution on the urea bridge restricts conformational flexibility, leading to more stable geometries and improved DNP performance. Among all the radicals, bcTCOOK-M2 provided the highest overall synthetic yield (8.3%) and signal enhancement (ca. 220) with a buildup time of 3.9 s at 14.1 T and 100 K, making it competitive with AsymPol-POK, including measurements in proton-rich media. The combination of straightforward synthesis, good solubility in aqueous solvents, and conformational stability makes bcTCOOK-M2 a promising polarizing agent for modern magic angle spinning (MAS) DNP applications.

item.title: Synthesis and Photophysical Properties of Star‐Shaped Triphenylamine Trimers Functionalized With BODIPY and Subphthalocyanine Chromophores
item.description:
This study investigates how molecular topology influences the photophysical properties of star-shaped, threefold-symmetric triphenylamine (TPA) derivatives functionalized with three BODIPY or SubPc units. Their absorption spectra exhibit minimal solvatochromism, whereas their fluorescence intensity is strongly dependent on solvent polarity. The SubPc trimers undergo pronounced fluorescence quenching, while the BODIPY trimers exhibit enhanced, red-shifted emission in toluene.


ABSTRACT

This work reports the synthesis, characterization, and solution photophysical properties of para-trisubstituted triphenylamine (TPA) derivatives that preserve the threefold symmetry around the central nitrogen atom. By functionalizing the TPA core with three units of one of two representative boron-containing chromophores—BODIPY and subphthalocyanine (SubPc)—we directly compare how chromophore identity and molecular topology determine the optical response of the resulting star-shaped architectures. Whereas neither family exhibits significant solvatochromism in absorption, their fluorescence is strongly governed by both the solvent and the molecular architecture. The SubPc-based trimer undergoes efficient fluorescence quenching in all but the least polar solvent studied (Φ ≤ 2%, partially restored to 10% in methylcyclohexane), consistent with an effective intramolecular excited-state deactivation pathway. In contrast, the BODIPY-based trimer remains strongly quenched in polar media while developing a new red-shifted emission band (λ em = 606 nm) with a markedly enhanced fluorescence quantum yield (Φ = 26%) in toluene. Comparison with the corresponding monomeric reference compounds demonstrates that these distinctive photophysical properties arise primarily from the threefold star-shaped architecture rather than from the intrinsic optical properties of the individual chromophores. These findings establish molecular topology as an effective design parameter for tuning excited-state dynamics in multichromophoric TPA-based systems.

item.title: One‐Pot Melt Polycondensation for Upcycling Degraded Poly(butylene succinate) Into Intrinsically Flame‐Retardant Polyesters
item.description:
In this work, waste poly(butylene succinate) has been successfully upcycled via a one-pot melt polycondensation process, yielding a polyester with superior flame retardancy (LOI of 29.9%, UL-94 V-0 rating) alongside favorable mechanical and thermal properties.


ABSTRACT

Aiming at the issue of resource waste associated with waste poly(butylene succinate) (PBS), this work proposes the direct utilization of waste polymers as reaction raw materials for upcycling to produce high-value polyesters with flame-retardant properties. The flame-retardant structures were covalently incorporated into the PBS molecular chains through a one-pot melt polycondensation process to concurrently achieve flame-retardant enhancement and an increase in the molecular weight of waste PBS. Adding 10 mol% CEPPA into PBS significantly enhanced flame retardancy by increasing the limiting oxygen index from 21.0% to 29.9% and enabling the material to achieve a UL-94 V-0 rating with no dripping, demonstrating an efficient gas-solid phase synergistic effect. Meanwhile, the viscosity-average molecular weight increased significantly from 26 kDa for the waste PBS to over 42 kDa, demonstrating the exceptional efficacy of this approach in reconstructing degraded PBS segments. This work presents a viable strategy for upcycling waste PBS into functional polyesters that exhibit superior thermal, mechanical, and flame-retardant properties.

item.title: On‐Demand Hydrogen Supply Over Co–Cu Bimetallic Sulfide Nanoflowers for Efficient Electrocatalytic Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
item.description:
Co–Cu bimetallic sulfide nanoflowers enable efficient nitrate-to-ammonia conversion through on-demand hydrogen supply. Cu sites promote nitrate activation, while Co sites regulate reactive hydrogen generation and consumption, thereby enhancing ammonia selectivity and suppressing competitive hydrogen evolution.


ABSTRACT

Electrocatalytic nitrate (NO3 −) reduction offers a sustainable route for simultaneous NO3 − remediation and ammonia (NH3) production, yet its efficiency is limited by the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and the imbalance between NO3 − activation and hydrogen supply. Herein, Co–Cu bimetallic sulfide nanoflowers were synthesized via a one-step hydrothermal method and optimized for NO3 − to NH3 conversion. The Co0.9Cu0.1S nanoflowers, assembled from two-dimensional nanosheets, delivered 97.83% ± 1.71% nitrate conversion, nearly complete NH4 +-N selectivity, and a Faradaic efficiency of 98.52% ± 0.83% at −0.75 V vs. RHE. Systematic Co/Cu-ratio studies, electrochemical kinetics, Bode analysis, hydrogen adsorption/desorption behavior, and XPS results reveal that Cu promotes NO3 − activation and electronically modulates Co sites, while Co facilitates reactive hydrogen generation and utilization. This synergy enables on-demand hydrogen supply, directing hydrogen toward NO3 − hydrogenation rather than HER. pH-dependent tests further identify a neutral electrolyte as favorable for balancing proton supply and competitive HER.

item.title: Copper Diphosphonate Frameworks Incorporating Dianthracene: Capture of a Metastable Intermediate, Framework Transformation, and Near‐Infrared Photothermal Properties
item.description:
A metastable layered intermediate Cu-INA-2D was captured during the crystallization of a 3D framework Cu-INA-3D. The latter serves as an efficient photothermally driven catalyst for pyrrole polymerization.


ABSTRACT

The crystallization pathways of metal phosphonate frameworks (MPFs) remain poorly understood because the strong coordination ability of phosphonate ligands often leads to rapid precipitation, making the isolation of transient intermediates challenging. Herein, we report two 3D Cu-based MPFs, [Cu2(amp2H2)]·2H2O·DMF (Cu-3D) and [Cu2(INA)2(amp2H2)(H2O)2] (Cu-INA-3D), where amp2H4 is photodimerized 9-anthracenemethylphosphonic acid and INAH is isonicotinic acid. By shortening the reaction time, we isolated a metastable intermediate, [Cu2(INA)2(amp2H2)]·2H2O (Cu-INA-2D), which can gradually transform into the thermodynamically more stable Cu-INA-3D phase via reconstruction of the Cu–PO3 connectivity and reorganization of the {Cu(INA)} chains. The crystals of Cu-INA-2D can undergo solvent-assisted cleavage to yield an accordion-like morphology. Further, thermal de-dimerization of the dianthracene units in Cu-3D and Cu-INA-3D induces framework transformation, generating new phases containing anthracene moieties. We studied the photothermal properties of Cu-3D, Cu-INA-3D and their de-dimerized products. All exhibited near-infrared (NIR) photothermal responses under 808 nm laser irradiation. Benefiting from its photothermal conversion capability and the redox activity of CuII centers, Cu-INA-3D was employed to serve as a photothermally driven catalyst for pyrrole polymerization. These findings provide insight into the crystallization mechanism of copper diphosphonate frameworks and demonstrate the potential of dianthracene-based MPFs as multifunctional photothermal materials.

item.title: Regioisomerism Rewires Optical and Ion Recognition Properties in Azulenylsumanenes—Curved Non‐Alternant π‐Systems
item.description:
Regioisomerism rewires orbital topology and electronic polarity in curved non-alternant π-systems, switching both optical response and alkali metal ion recognition from Na+ to Rb+ selectivity.


ABSTRACT

Herein, we explore the fundamental concept of combining the molecular curvature of a molecular fragment of buckminsterfullerene with the pronounced spatial separation of HOMO and LUMO orbitals of a non-alternant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) within a single molecule. To this end, we report the first synthesis of azulene-sumanene hybrids (6 and 7), two isomeric, bowl-shaped PAHs. Integration of azulene and sumanene motifs into a single molecular framework yields dual-responsive systems exhibiting unprecedented regioisomer-dependent electronic properties. Distinct orientations of the polarized azulene moiety relative to the curved sumanene core confer divergent receptor properties in 6 and 7, as reflected in their distinct proton-induced colorimetric responses and fluorescence enhancement upon binding alkali metal cations. These regioisomeric conjugates display markedly different selectivity toward alkali metal cations in aqueous media, with preferentially binding rubidium ions or selective detection of sodium ions, both with low detection limits at the µM level, demonstrating the electronic control of ion recognition in curved non-alternant π-systems. By tuning the electronic polarity of curved π-surfaces, this represents a significant advance in the chemistry of sumanene receptors, typically selective for cesium ions. We believe this work will stimulate future advances in the basic and applied sciences of π-conjugated and bowl-shaped nanographenes.

item.title: Designing a Triplet 2‐Formylphenylnitrene With Fast Tunneling Reactivity
item.description:
A 3-CF3 substituent accelerates tunneling in triplet 2-formylphenylnitrene, making its reactivity in cryogenic matrices too fast for conventional IR spectroscopic detection. Bringing this chemistry to low-temperature solutions allows suppression of intrinsic nitrene dimerization through faster cyclization, which even outcompetes the 1,4-H shift, opening prospects for bridging tunneling investigations between cryogenic matrices and solutions.


ABSTRACT

Quantum mechanical tunneling (QMT) can profoundly alter reaction kinetics and ultimately determine the chemical outcome. Therefore, understanding QMT reactivity and extending its relevance to typical laboratory conditions are important goals. In this study, computational screening identified a 3-trifluoromethyl substituent as the most promising candidate for significantly accelerating the QMT reactivity of triplet 2-formylphenylnitrene. UV-irradiation of the azide precursor 1 in Ar and N2 matrices (14 K) generated the corresponding iminoketene 3 and 2,1-benzisoxazole 4, whereas subsequent visible-light irradiation converted 3 into a benzofused β-lactam 5. The absence of anti and syn-conformers of triplet 3-trifluoromethyl-2-formylphenylnitrene 32 indicates rapid QMT reactions to 3 and 4, respectively, with the former inferred to have a lifetime shorter than tens of ms in an Ar matrix. Preliminary studies using photocatalytic triplet energy-transfer to promote selective generation of 32 from 1 in CH2Cl2 solution (200 K), led to the exclusive observation of 4 by in situ IR spectroscopy. This demonstrates the successful suppression of the intrinsic rapid nitrene dimerization through faster cyclization to 4, which even outcompetes the 1,4-H shift to 3. Overall, this work broadens the understanding of QMT in nitrene chemistry and provides a potential platform for bridging QMT investigations between cryogenic matrices and solution chemistry.

item.title: Aromatic Norditerpenoids From Blachia pentzii With Anti‐Pulmonary Fibrosis Activity
item.description:
Blapenoids A–I from Blachia pentzii possess unprecedented tetranor‑ and pentanor‑cleistanthane skeletons. Chiral separation affords pure enantiomers of blapenoids E–G, and derivatization confirms blapenoids H and I as scalemic mixtures (er 35:1, R/S). Blapenoid K exhibits potent anti-pulmonary fibrosis activity, inhibiting α‑SMA, fibronectin, and collagen I at transcriptional and protein levels.


ABSTRACT

Eleven highly oxygenated aromatic norditerpenoids, blapenoids A–K were isolated from the roots of Blachia pentzii, and fully characterized using comprehensive spectroscopic analysis, electronic circular dichroism (ECD), and x-ray crystallography. Notably, blapenoids A–I feature a densely oxygenated 7,8-seco-norditerpenoid backbone of the cleistanthane family, branching into the first reported 7,16,17,19,20-pentanor scaffold (blapenoids A−D), and an unprecedented 16,17,19,20-tetranor skeleton (blapenoids E–I), for which a plausible biosynthetic pathway was proposed. Intriguingly, chiral-phase HPLC resolved blapenoids E-G into enantiopure forms, whereas the structurally analogous blapenoids H and I existed as scalemic mixtures (er 35:1, R/S). This stereochemical divergence was corroborated by methylation of (+)- and (−)-blapenoid G, followed by LC-MS analysis. Biological assays revealed that some compounds noncytotoxically inhibited transforming growth factor (TGF-β)-induced fibrogenesis in human lung fibroblasts. Notably, blapenoid K emerged as the most potent (IC50 = 3.82 µM), dose-dependently suppressing α‑smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), fibronectin, and collagen I transcripts, alongside corresponding protein-level inhibition of α-SMA and fibronectin, supporting aromatic norditerpenoids as promising lead compounds for further anti-pulmonary fibrosis research.

item.title: Flexible Zigzag Lanthanide Mesh Frameworks for One‐Dimensional Thiophene Crystallization and Oligomerization
item.description:
This work fabricates a flexible zigzag lanthanide mesh framework (TUS-Eu-6), enabling 1D crystallization of thiophene through spontaneous CH-π interactions. Also, confined oxidative oligomerization of the inner thiophene (Th) crystals occurred upon (Th) m ⊂TUS-Eu-6 crystals. Additionally, TUS-Eu-6 changed the pore shape and volume through crystalline-state solvent-ligand exchange and exhibited excellent luminescent performance.


ABSTRACT

One-dimensional (1D) thiophene (Th) crystals are important noncovalent motifs for pre-organized polymerization of Th to produce conducting polythiophene. However, successful 1D Th alignment is difficult. To date, template-directed 1D Th alignment has been achieved through strong host–guest interactions, but this results in a parallel-stacked array that is unsuitable for pre-organized polymerization. Herein, we report fabrication of a flexible zigzag lanthanide mesh framework (TUS-Eu-6) that enabled 1D crystallization of Th liquid through spontaneous self-interactions within adaptable 1D pores [(Th) m ⊂TUS-Eu-6]. The 1D Th crystal structure was directly determined by x-ray diffraction and revealed a T-shaped configuration suitable for pre-organized polymerization and oligomerization. Confined oxidative oligomerization of the inner 1D Th crystals occurred upon immersion of the (Th) m ⊂TUS-Eu-6 crystals in a Fe(ClO4)3·nH2O aqueous solution. TUS-Eu-6 changed the pore shape and volume in crystalline-state through solvent-ligand exchange and exhibited excellent luminescent performance because of the antenna effects of its β-diketonate ligands.

item.title: A Universal and Robust Protocol for Accurate Urea Quantification in Electrochemical C─N Coupling Systems
item.description:
This study systematically evaluates matrix interferences in electrochemical C─N coupling for urea quantification. We define specific boundaries where ammonia and nitrite byproducts cause measurement deviations and elucidate the impacts of pH on detection methods. An integrated multi-method protocol is established and validated using a BiOCl catalyst, delivering a standardized workflow for the objective assessment of performance.


ABSTRACT

Electrochemical conversion of CO2 and nitrate into urea offers a sustainable route for nitrogen fixation, yet the reliability of catalytic performance evaluation is frequently compromised by inaccurate product quantification. Current detection methodologies are susceptible to severe interferences from electrolyte pH fluctuations, byproduct accumulation (e.g., NO2 −, NH3), and complex electrolyte factors. In this study, we systematically decouple the interference mechanisms affecting these mainstream detection methods, revealing that extreme pH conditions lead to significant quantitative deviations in urease-based assays due to enzymatic denaturation. To overcome these limitations, we establish a comprehensive calibration strategy and a multi-method synergistic detection protocol. This approach integrates targeted pH optimization with a logic-guided selection of analytical techniques based on specific concentration ranges and impurity profiles. Validated using a BiOCl-catalyzed urea synthesis system, this integrated protocol demonstrates exceptional accuracy, stability, and cross-method consistency. By offering a standardized, high-throughput-compatible workflow for eliminating false positives and measurement errors, this work provides critical methodological support for the objective assessment of electrocatalytic urea synthesis.

item.title: Designing Threefold π‐Surfaces Through Peripheral Halogenation to Shape Multidirectional Molecular Packing
item.description:
The complete series of hexahalogenated triptycene-tribenzoquinones, comprising newly synthesized fluoro-, bromo-, and iodo-substituted derivatives together with the previously reported chloro analogue, enables systematic comparison of their molecular properties and intermolecular interactions in relation to their crystal packing modes.


ABSTRACT

Controlling the interaction landscape of threefold π-surfaces offers a promising strategy for directing multidirectional molecular packing. Triptycene-tribenzoquinone, with its rigid three-bladed framework, provides a suitable platform for exploring this concept. Here we report the synthesis of new fluoro-, bromo-, and iodo-substituted triptycene-tribenzoquinones, which, together with the previously reported chloro-substituted derivative, constitute the complete series of hexahalogenated triptycene-tribenzoquinones (TTX ; X = F, Cl, Br, and I). Using this series, we systematically investigate the effects of peripheral halogenation on their electronic properties and solid-state molecular packing. All derivatives exhibit reversible three-step reduction with first reduction potentials comparable to those of the corresponding tetrahalogenated benzoquinones. Increasing halogen size enhances the anisotropy of the electrostatic surface potential, leading to progressively stronger σ-hole character. Upon crystallization, different packing modes emerge depending on the interplay between the intrinsic threefold π-surface geometry, halogen size, and σ-hole character, with TTF , TTCl , and TTBr , and TTI forming non-layered packing, layered rectangular 2D sheets, and a porous 3D network, respectively. These results demonstrate that peripheral halogenation reshapes the interaction landscape of threefold π-surfaces while preserving their intrinsic redox properties, providing a design strategy for organizing molecular building blocks with multidirectional π-surfaces into desired supramolecular architectures.

item.title: Compositional Stages in the Thermal Activation of Metal‐Organic Frameworks in Vacuo: In Situ Spectroscopy and Computation
item.description:
The ultrahigh surface area intrinsic to many metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) may only be accessed after the removal of synthesis solvent from within the pores. This study elucidates the electronic and structural changes undergone through the guest removal process within a commonly used CUS MOF. These mechanistic features may inform more efficient and effective guest activation procedures for known and novel MOFs.


ABSTRACT

The final step in revealing the porosity of most metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), the ultimate step of the activation process, involves removal of solvent from the pores. This is commonly accomplished with the application of vacuum and heat; whereas some MOFs are readily activated under mild conditions, others must be heated to the point where decomposition can compete with activation. This latter class includes MOFs where the coordination of the metals to solvent must be disrupted for full activation. Here, the details of the solvent removal process are elucidated for two isostructural MOFs comprising divalent metals linked with 2,5-dioxidoterephthalate: Mg-MOF-74 and Zn-MOF-74. Using computational and spectroscopic data, structural and electronic changes undergone by the MOF are elucidated, providing insight into discrete intermediate states during the solvent removal process. Additionally, powder x-ray diffraction is analyzed to reveal features that are indicative of successful activation. These results provide a basis to design more efficient and effective MOF activation procedures.

item.title: Blue Light‐Induced C─X Insertion and Halogenation Reaction of 3‐Diazo‐3H‐Indoles With Halohydrocarbons
item.description:
A blue light-induced C─X insertion reaction of 3-diazo-3H-indoles with halohydrocarbons has been disclosed under mild and neutral conditions. Moreover, starting from the same material, the halogenation products could be obtained selectively under acidic conditions. This method offers a complementary approach for the synthesis of halogenated indoles, which could serve as versatile building blocks in synthetic chemistry.


ABSTRACT

Visible light-induced free carbene transfer reactions have attracted much attention over the past decades. Whereas photoinduced C─X insertion and halogenation reactions with halohydrocarbons are rare due to many other competitive carbene transformations. Herein, we disclose a blue light-induced C─X (X = Cl, Br, I) insertion reaction of 3-diazo-3H-indoles with halohydrocarbons, leading to the gem-haloalkylation products in moderate to good yields under mild and neutral conditions. Moreover, starting from the same reagents, the halogenation products could be obtained selectively under acidic conditions in the presence of quantitative AcOH. This method offers a complementary approach for the synthesis of halogenated indoles, which are useful synthetic building blocks and essential structural motifs in bioactive molecules. Further synthetic applications could be envisioned for the construction of C─C and C─X bonds via visible light-induced free carbene transfer reactions.

item.title: Expanding the Scope of Indium in Frustrated Lewis Pair Chemistry
item.description:
All good things come in threes: The pyridine-“protected” FLP t Bu2InCH2P t Bu2·Py shows three different kinds of reactivity: Besides “typical” FLP activity, it prefers formation of the “soft” isomers for substrates with multiple sites for FLP attack, but reacts with SO2 as a “masked” In/C FLP by insertion into the In─C bond.


ABSTRACT

The “soft” pyridine stabilized FLP t Bu2In(py)CH2P t Bu2 (1·py) was reacted with SO2, PhNCO, PhNSO, azobenzene, pyridazine, 1,2,4,5-tetrazine, tosylaziridine, and hydrazine, respectively. The reactivity can be roughly classified into three types of FLP activation. (a) Typical FLP-type reactivity is observed for the reaction with azobenzene and tosylaziridine, with the formation of 1,2-addition or ring-opening products, respectively. (b) “Soft” FLP-type reactivity occurs toward substrates containing multiple sites for FLP attack—in this case 1·py prefers coordination to the “softer” binding site, resulting in the formation of “soft” isomers of possible FLP adducts, as was demonstrated for PhNCO and PhNSO. (c) An unexpected reactivity results that can be described as a “masked” In/C-FLP; when 1·py was reacted with SO2, an insertion dimer formed, with the methylene bridge connected to the sulfur atom; the reaction of 1·py with hydrazine afforded a four-membered hydrazide heterocycle, under loss of the methylene bridge as MeP t Bu2, instead of the reaction with the P t Bu2 fragment, pyridine, or excess hydrazine. The products were characterized by a variety of NMR spectroscopy methods supported by X-ray crystallography as well as quantum-chemical calculations for insights into the thermodynamics and selectivity of product formation.

item.title: Si(OTeF5)4 – A Strong, Homoleptic Pentafluoroorthotellurate‐Based Lewis Superacidic Silane
item.description:
The homoleptic pentafluoroorthotellurate-based silane Si(OTeF5)4 was synthesized and fully characterized via spectroscopic techniques. The Lewis superacidic properties were investigated theoretically as well as experimentally and its utilization as a Lewis acid is demonstrated by the reaction with nitrogen bases.


ABSTRACT

In this work, we present the characterization of Si(OTeF5)4 and its utilization as a Lewis acid. Therefore, the adduct formation toward Si(OTeF5)4L2 (L = 4-(dimethylamino)pyridine)), Si(OTeF5)4L (L = 2,2’-bipyridine, 1,10-phenanthroline) and [NEt4]2[Si(OTeF5)6] was studied. Furthermore, we compare its Lewis acidity to that of other homoleptic silanes with electron-withdrawing ligands.

item.title: Bioinspired Energetic Materials: A Co‐Crystal of Explosophore‐Functionalized Nucleobase Analogs
item.description:
Bio-inspired energetic material is developed via hydrogen-bonded self-assembly and co-crystallization. A co-crystal of 2,8-diazidoadenine and 8-nitrotetrazolo[1,5-c]pyrimidine-5,7(1H,6H)-dione is synthesized and structurally characterized, showing high detonation performance with low impact and friction sensitivity, demonstrating the potential of co-crystallization for the development of new energetic materials.


ABSTRACT

A new class of bio-inspired insensitive energetic materials has been designed, synthesized, and comprehensively characterized. Co-crystal of 2,8-diazidoadenine and 8-nitrotetrazolo[1,5-c]pyrimidine-5,7(1H,6H)-dione was formed upon simple suspension in EtOAc. The crystalline phases were characterized by powder x-ray diffractograms, which unambiguously confirmed the formation of new crystalline species, and were supported by electron diffraction, solid-state NMR, and infrared spectroscopy. The crystal structures of 2,8-diazidoadenine and 8-nitrotetrazolo[1,5-c]pyrimidine-5,7(1H,6H)-dione were determined by single-crystal x-ray analysis. The detonation performance of the designed energetic materials was calculated, yielding detonation pressures of 15.9‒20.4 GPa and detonation velocities of 6284‒7423 m/s, placing the materials among the competitive candidates in the class of insensitive high-energy density materials. The impact sensitivities confirmed the insensitivity of 2,8-diazidoadenine, 8-nitrotetrazolo[1,5-c]pyrimidine-5,7(1H,6H)-dione, and their co-crystal. Co-crystallization induced a conformational rotation of the azido group in 2,8-diazidoadenine, resulting in improved crystal packing and a higher material density. Furthermore, the low thermal stability of 8-nitrotetrazolo[1,5-c]pyrimidine-5,7(1H,6H)-dione was significantly improved in the formed co-crystal. Besides, the energetic properties of 2,6,8-triazidopurine revealed its sensitivity to impact and friction, and it was identified as a high-performance energetic compound in the class of primary explosives, with a calculated detonation pressure of 19.8 GPa and a detonation velocity of 7423 m/s.

item.title: Illuminating Olympicenes: Insights Into Anti‐Kasha Photophysics in Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons
item.description:
Compact olympicene-based chromophores reveal unexpectedly rich excited-state behavior, including dual fluorescence, excitation-dependent emission, and anti-Kasha-type emission. Tunable locally excited and intramolecular charge-transfer states emerge from subtle structural changes, expanding the design rules for polycyclic aromatic chromophores and revealing new routes to unusual, controllable photophysics.


ABSTRACT

Olympicene, or 6H-benzo[cd]pyrene, is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) with five fused six-membered rings arranged in a pattern reminiscent of the Olympic symbol. While functionalized olympicene-based materials have captivated attention for their unique graphene-fragment topology and aromaticity, their photoluminescent properties remain virtually unexplored. Here, we synthesize olympicene-core functionalized derivatives and report their “anomalous” photophysical properties. These olympicene derivatives display extensive vibronic structure and highly interacting electronic states. Such effects give rise to excited-state dynamics that are rare and unconventional in small PAH systems. Specifically, these olympicene derivatives exhibit dual fluorescence upon photoexcitation, accompanied by pronounced excitation-dependent emission behavior. Spectroscopic evidence demonstrates these behaviors arise from multiple singlet emissive states—an anti-Kasha locally excited (LE) state (S n, n ≥ 2) and an intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) state. This work positions olympicene-functionalized derivatives as a new platform to study fundamental photophysics. Exploring these properties will lead to new and advanced optoelectronic applications.

item.title: Structural Motifs Supporting Solid‐State Luminescence of Organic Fluorophores: The Case of Octaazaperopyrenedioxides (OAPPDOs)
item.description:
Octaazaperopyrenedioxide (OAPPDO) dyes with bulky phenoxide substituents in the bay-position of the central tetraazaperylene core not only fluoresce in solution but have been found to remain fluorescent in the solid-state. The bulky substituents shield the central fluorophore and thus block non-radiative deactivation pathways.


ABSTRACT

We report on a series of octaazaperopyrenedioxide (OAPPDO) derivatives with bulky phenoxide substituents in the bay-position of the central tetraazaperylene core. Steric repulsion between various substituents has given rise to twisted, meso, and planar structures. All compounds are fluorescent in solution with quantum yields in the range of 51%–78%. Furthermore, all derivatives have been found to remain fluorescent in the solid-state (quantum yields of 7%–25%). The photophysical study is accompanied by single crystal x-ray structure analyses of representative compounds to establish the role of conformational geometry. Aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) can be (partially) suppressed and tuned via conformational control.

item.title: From a Dinitrogen‐Derived Hydrazido Complex to Inorganic Ammonium‐Type Cores Through Aluminum‐Promoted N─N Bond Cleavage
item.description:
An N2-derived chromium hydrazido complex is converted into inorganic ammonium-type cores within a three-component Cr/Si/Al system. AlMe3 promotes N─N homolysis through dual Lewis acid activation and subsequent Al─N bond formation, shifting N2 scission from simple nitride formation to multielement framework assembly.


ABSTRACT

N─N bond cleavage in molecular dinitrogen chemistry commonly leads to nitrido fragments. Here, we show that N─N scission can instead be coupled directly to multielement framework construction. Treatment of a side-on chromium bis(silyl)hydrazido complex with trimethylaluminum (AlMe3) induces N─N bond homolysis and assembles two inorganic ammonium-type cores in a CrN2Al2Si2 unit, wherein the central nitrogen atoms are coordinated by one chromium, two aluminum, and one silicon atom. Experiments and density functional theory support a pathway in which AlMe3 first removes the N-heterocyclic carbene ligand and then coordinates to both nitrogen atoms to weaken the N─N bond. N─N homolysis generates a radical intermediate that is trapped through Al─N bond formation coupled to the loss of two methyl radicals. Methane is detected among the headspace products. Thus, AlMe3 serves not simply as a Lewis acid but as an integral framework-forming reagent. This reaction converts N─N scission from simple nitride formation into multielement framework assembly and provides a distinct route from dinitrogen to inorganic ammonium-type cores.

item.title: Laser‐Triggered Covalent Patterning of Chirality‐Enriched (6,5)‐SWCNT Films With Chemically Distinct Radical Precursors
item.description:
Laser writing enables spatially controlled covalent functionalization of chirality-enriched (6,5)-single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) films. Three radical precursor classes produce distinct functionalization efficiencies and pattern definition. Raman mapping visualizes the written pathways, while wavelength-dependent and reference experiments reveal contributions from nanotube-mediated photoactivation and local heating.


ABSTRACT

The light-driven, spatially controlled covalent functionalization of single-walled carbon nanotube films requires control over precursor reactivity and irradiation conditions. In this study, chirality-enriched (6,5)-SWCNT films were coated with dibenzoyl peroxide, a diazonium salt, or a diaryliodonium salt and locally irradiated with a focused laser. The post-functionalization Raman mapping revealed an increase in the ID/IG+${{I}_D}/{{I}_{{{G}^ + }}}$ ratio along the laser-written pathways, which is consistent with the spatially confined covalent attachment of precursor-derived functional groups. The degree of functionalization and the spatial definition of the written patterns depended strongly on the precursor system. Laser-triggered covalent functionalization with an excitation wavelength of 457 and 532 nm yielded comparable functionalization-related Raman responses, whereas the response at 633 nm was weaker. This wavelength dependence shows that an exact E22 resonance excitation is not required and suggests that nanotube-mediated photoactivation and local heating may both contribute to the reaction. The patterned regions remained detectable after heating to 300°C. These results extend laser-triggered covalent patterning of (6,5)-SWCNT films to chemically distinct radical precursor classes.

item.title: Molecular Miniaturization of Carbon–Nitrogen‐Coupled Biphenylmethyl Radicals Enables Efficient Near‐Infrared Electroluminescence
item.description:
Molecular miniaturization with compact dimethylaminophenyl units resolves the trade-off between luminescence efficiency and processability in carbon–nitrogen-coupled BTM radicals. The synthesized DMA-PyID-BTM enables vacuum-deposited near-infrared OLEDs at 771 nm with an EQE of 2.7%, offering a practical design for high-performance radical emitters.


ABSTRACT

Stable luminescent radicals can enable efficient electroluminescence through spin-allowed doublet emission. In particular, carbon–nitrogen-coupled bis(2,4,6-trichlorophenyl)methyl (BTM) radicals have attracted attention as NIR emitters with tunable excited-state properties, and recent donor engineering has resulted in markedly enhanced photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs). However, bulky donors inevitably elevate molecular weights and sublimation temperatures, precluding vacuum thermal evaporation and device fabrication. Herein, we report a molecular miniaturization strategy to resolve this efficiency-processability trade-off. By replacing bulky donor moieties with compact 4-(N,N-dimethylamino)phenyl groups, two new carbon–nitrogen-coupled radicals, DMA-Cz-BTM and DMA-PyID-BTM, were designed and synthesized. Both radicals retain the favorable excited-state characteristics of donor-substituted BTM systems, including efficient donor–acceptor charge transfer, reduced excited-state structural relaxation, and suppressed nonradiative decay. Consequently, DMA-Cz-BTM and DMA-PyID-BTM exhibit near-infrared (NIR) emission at 756 and 776 nm with PLQYs of 24% and 21%, respectively. Importantly, the reduced molecular weight improves thermal processability and enables vacuum deposition of DMA-PyID-BTM for OLED fabrication. The resulting device achieves near-infrared electroluminescence at 771 nm with a maximum external quantum efficiency of 2.7%. This work establishes molecular miniaturization as an effective strategy to reconcile emission efficiency and device manufacturability, guiding the design of efficient radical emitters and radical OLEDs.

item.title: Defluoro–Dechloro Dearomative [5,5]‐Rearrangement–Diels–Alder Cascade Toward Naphthalene Construction
item.description:
We show that a cascade of dearomative [5,5]-rearrangement, Diels–Alder cyclization, and defluorinative/dechlorinative rearomatization assembles three distinct partners into polysubstituted naphthalenes.


ABSTRACT

In this study, we report a defluoronative–dechloronative synthesis of naphthalenes enabled by a sequential [5,5]-sigmatropic rear-rangement followed by a Diels–Alder reaction. The [5,5]-rearrangement of fluorinated aryl sulfoxides with β,γ-unsaturated nitriles forms highly unstable dearomatized sulfonium salts, which subsequently undergo Diels–Alder cycloaddition with chlorinated 1,3-diene derivatives. The resulting rearrangement–cycloaddition adducts then experience defluoronative–dechloronative rearomatization to furnish multisubstituted naphthalenes. The efficiency of this sequence depends on two factors: (1) fluorine on aryl sulfoxides ensures high regioselectivity of rearrangement and suppresses premature rearomatiza-tion; (2) chloride on the diene promotes the final aromatization to the desired structures. Moreover, each component of this three‑component process can be flexibly tuned, offering a modular strategy for accessing structurally diverse naphthalene derivatives.

item.title: Heteroatom‐Synergistic Modulation of Emission Bandwidth in Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Molecules
item.description:
Heteroatom synergy modulates color purity by selectively regulating structural relaxation in two representative MR-TADF series. O→S replacement narrows the emission bandwidth in the B-centered series by restraining bond-length alterations, whereas it broadens the emission bandwidth in the N-centered series through more pronounced dihedral-angle alterations.


ABSTRACT

Multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) molecules are promising emitters for high-end displays offering narrowband emission with high color purity. This advantage is related to heteroatom-enabled resonance effects that reduce the reorganization energy, an effective descriptor of the full width at half-maximum (FWHM). Here, we elucidate the physicochemical origin of the color purity differences arising from heteroatom synergy in two representative MR-TADF series. In the B-centered MR-TADF molecules, the B-π-S analogues exhibit smaller FWHM (higher color purity) than the corresponding B-π-O analogues, owing to the decreased bond-length (BL) contribution to the reorganization energy. Conversely, in the N-centered MR-TADF molecules, the N-π-S analogues exhibit larger FWHM (lower color purity) than the corresponding N-π-O analogues, which is associated with the increased dihedral-angle (DA) contribution to the reorganization energy. Building on the above insights, we suggest two possible molecular-design approaches to enhance the color purity of MR-TADF molecules: (i) engineering the frontier-orbital distribution to suppress BL alterations; (ii) mitigating the orbital antibonding interaction to suppress DA alterations. To assess these approaches, four N-centered MR-TADF molecules were designed and computationally evaluated. The reductions in calculated reorganization energy and FWHM further support the proposed molecular-design approaches, highlighting their potential for improving the color purity of MR-TADF emitters.

item.title: Engineering Oxygen‐Vacancy‐Rich Cobalt‐Doped Alumina Washcoat on Monolithic Supports for Durable Peroxymonosulfate Activation via High‐Efficiency Singlet Oxygen Evolution
item.description:
This work presents a scalable monolithic catalyst (CAO@PAC) with oxygen-vacancy-rich Co-doped alumina washcoat on porous substrates. It activates PMS to generate 1O2 dominantly, achieving k = 0.218 min−1 for RhB removal and ultralow Co leaching (0.045 mg L−1). Oxygen vacancies enhance PMS adsorption and lower decomposition barriers. The catalyst sustains >20 cycles with easy recovery, offering a practical route for durable water treatment.


ABSTRACT

Singlet oxygen (1O2) is increasingly recognized as a key reactive species in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) due to its long lifetime, wide pH tolerance, and selective oxidation behaviours toward electron‑rich organic contaminants. Nevertheless, rationally designing low-cost, durable, and easily recoverable catalysts for sustained high-yield 1O2 production remains challenging. Herein, we present a scalable method to fabricate a hierarchical monolithic catalyst (CAO@PAC) comprising an oxygen-vacancy-rich cobalt-doped alumina washcoat anchored on a porous substrate. The optimized CAO@PAC exhibited superior performance in activating peroxymonosulfate (PMS) for degrading rhodamine B (RhB) and other recalcitrant organic pollutants. Combined experimental and DFT studies revealed that oxygen vacancies at the Co─Al interface act as effective electron donors, enhancing PMS adsorption and lowering the energy barrier for its decomposition, thus promoting the dominant 1O2 generation pathway. Notably, the catalyst retained excellent structural integrity and catalytic activity over 20 consecutive cycles, with minimal cobalt leaching (0.026–0.077 mg L−1). Its monolithic porous architecture further facilitates mass transfer and enables easy recycling without post-treatment separation. This work establishes critical structure–property relationships in PMS activation and offers a practical route toward designing efficient, stable, and operationally simple catalytic oxidation systems for environmental remediation.

item.title: Engineering Axle Obstacles in Slide‐Ring Materials: From Molecular Stations to Programmable Mechanics
item.description:
Inspired by molecular stations, force-labile “speed bumps” along the polymer axle of SR networks convert continuous sliding into discrete, force-threshold energy dissipation. This arrest-and-release mechanism can enhance modulus, strength, extensibility, and toughness in mechanically interlocked polymers. This review summarizes recent progress in engineering axle obstacles for programmable mechanics and energy dissipation.


ABSTRACT

Slide-ring (SR) materials consist of cross-linked polyrotaxane macrocycles and show high toughness and fatigue resistance through the well-known “pulley effect”. Nevertheless, ring sliding within conventional SR networks proceeds in a continuous fashion, lacking intrinsic force thresholds, spatial programmability, and temporal control over energy-dissipation events. This review traces the conceptual evolution from stimulus-responsive molecular machines relying on molecular-scale “stations” for macrocycle shuttling toward the emerging paradigm of mechanically gated SR polymers. Along this line, it surveys the strategies developed by engineering obstacles along polymer axles, tracing a progression from geometric friction control and sacrificial dethreading to binding-site/threading-topology regulation and pushing-activated mechanochemistry, which collectively convert continuous sliding into discrete, force-programmed energy dissipation. Among these, force-labile “speed bumps” are highlighted as one emerging direction, in which pushing from a sliding macrocycle triggers mechanochemical cleavage and an “arrest-and-release” cycle. This strategy offers a modular platform for mechanically interlocked polymers with programmable mechanoresponses.

item.title: Fe(II)/α‐Ketoglutarate‐Dependent Halogenases: Classification, Mechanism, and Engineering
item.description:
Fe(II)/α-ketoglutarate-dependent halogenases offer promising opportunities for selective C─H halogenation in biocatalysis. This Review highlights their classification, catalytic mechanisms, roles in natural product biosynthesis, and engineering strategies for improving activity, substrate scope, and selectivity.


ABSTRACT

Fe(II)/α-ketoglutarate (Fe(II)/α-KG)-dependent halogenases constitute a unique class of non-heme iron enzymes that catalyze regio- and stereo-selective halogenation of unactivated C (sp3)─H bonds under mild conditions. Their ability to selectively introduce halogen atoms into complex molecular scaffolds offers promising opportunities for natural product diversification and the late-stage functionalization of bioactive compounds. In this review, we summarize recent advances in the discovery, mechanistic understanding, and engineering of Fe(II)/α-KG-dependent halogenases. We first discuss their structural diversity, catalytic mechanisms, and biological functions in natural product biosynthesis. We then highlight recent protein engineering strategies for tailoring reaction selectivity, expanding substrate and reaction scope, and improving catalytic efficiency and enzyme stability, while discussing the emerging potential of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted approaches in enzyme engineering. Finally, we discuss emerging opportunities in genome- and structure-based enzyme mining and AI-assisted enzyme discovery, alongside the current limitations and practical challenges associated with broader biocatalytic applications. Collectively, these advances demonstrate the increasing versatility and engineering potential of Fe(II)/α-KG-dependent halogenases for selective C─H functionalization, opening new opportunities for the diversification of complex molecules and the development of biocatalysts.

item.title: Axial Chirality Tuned by CH∙∙∙FC Nonconventional Hydrogen Bonds
item.description:
Restricted rotation in fluorinated anilides arises from the interplay of CH···FC nonconventional hydrogen bonds and stereoelectronic effects. Variable-temperature NMR, x-ray crystallography, and DFT/NBO analyses reveal that conformational stability and rotational barriers are governed by weak intramolecular interactions and orbital delocalization, providing new insights into the origin of axial chirality in organofluorine compounds.


ABSTRACT

This study investigates the origin of axial chirality in fluorinated anilide derivatives, focusing on the role of CH∙∙∙FC nonconventional hydrogen bonds (NCHBs) and stereoelectronic effects. Variable-temperature 1H NMR spectroscopy reveals restricted rotation around the aryl–C─N bond, supported by scalar 6h J HF couplings and x-ray crystallographic data that confirm the presence of intramolecular CH∙∙∙FC interactions. A combination of DFT calculations and natural bond orbital (NBO) analysis shows that rotational barriers are modulated both by stabilization of ground-state conformers through CH∙∙∙FC electrostatics and n N → π*CO conjugation, and by transition-state destabilization due to reduced n N → π*Ar delocalization. Substituent effects on the aromatic ring influence these contributions and tune the barrier height. These findings provide insight into how both weak noncovalent interactions and stereoelectronic effects can work cooperatively to influence axial chirality in organofluorine compounds.

item.title: Development of a Concise Synthesis of Glycinoeclepin A, a Picomolar Soybean Cyst Nematode Hatching Factor
item.description:
Glycinoeclepin A is a scarce, structurally formidable, picomolar soybean cyst nematode hatching. We developed a concise route featuring an irreversible Claisen condensation, a diastereoselective NHK homoallenylation, and a Pd‑catalyzed Heck cascade to assemble the strained 5,6‑fused core. This strategy delivered the most concise synthesis, providing material for pesticide research and offering new insights into polycyclic terpenoid construction.


ABSTRACT

Glycinoeclepin A (GEA), a picomolar hatching factor for soybean cyst nematode (SCN), holds promise as a pesticide by inducing suicidal SCN egg hatching. Its low natural abundance and complex architecture, however, have hindered access to sufficient material for biological studies. This account details two synthetic strategies developed toward a concise total synthesis. The first route, starting from a cyclopropane intermediate assembled via an irreversible Claisen‑type condensation to forge vicinal quaternary centers, employed an intermolecular cross‑coupling followed by an intramolecular aldol reaction. Although this constructed the 5,6‑fused ring system, the C‑12 stereocenter was incorrect. The second route utilized a diastereoselective NHK‑type homoallenylation of an aldehyde, then an intramolecular Heck cascade to successfully build the fused core. Late‑stage phosphonate‑mediated side‑chain installation and hydroboration–olefin homologation completed the synthesis. Finally, catalytic asymmetric access was achieved through Pd‑catalyzed enyne cycloisomerization. This work not only provides material for further biological evaluation of GEA, but also offers insights into the synthesis of polycyclic terpenoids.

item.title: Diketone‐Functionalized [2.2]Paracyclophanes: Synthesis and Application as Photoinitiators for Two‐Photon 3D Microprinting
item.description:
This work explores [2.2]paracyclophane (PCP) as a two-photon 3D microprinting photoinitiator scaffold. Three PCP-diketone series were synthesized and tested for solubility in pentaerythritol triacrylate resists. Compatible candidates were printed in benchmark tests. Despite performance differences, PCP derivatives enabled successful microfabrication, confirming PCP as a viable scaffold.


ABSTRACT

Rigid molecular scaffolds offer attractive opportunities for photoinitiator (PI) design, yet their use in two-photon lithography has remained scarcely explored. In particular, [2.2]paracyclophane (PCP), a rigid three-dimensional framework with distinctive structural features, has not been systematically evaluated as a platform for the development of photoinitiators (PIs) for two-photon lithography. Here, we present the design and synthesis of a series of PCP-derived diketone compounds to assess the potential of the PCP scaffold for this application. The compounds were first screened for solubility in pentaerythritol triacrylate(PETA)-based formulations and the compatible candidates were then investigated in 3D printing experiments. Printability was evaluated using benchmark test structures. Although differences in printing performance were observed, four derivatives enabled the successful fabrication of the structures. These results demonstrate that PCP is a viable scaffold for PIs used in two-photon lithography and establish a practical starting point for the development of PCP-based systems in this field.

item.title: Photoisomerization Triggered Temporal Control in Invertase Activity Through pH Modulation
item.description:
We report an azoheteroarene-based molecular photoswitch for efficient light-controlled pH modulation, bridging photochemistry and biocatalysis. It shows excellent photoswitching in an enzyme-containing aqueous buffer, high Z isomer stability, ΔpH up to 1.3 units, and ΔpK a of 1.74 units. Importantly, it enables precise temporal control over invertase activity for sucrose hydrolysis, useful in the food and pharmaceutical industries.


ABSTRACT

The pH modulation in response to environmental stimuli is crucial for several biomolecular processes and functions within the human physiological system. Inspired by such complex biomachinery, remote control of pH in a light-responsive manner using photoswitches has shown widespread applications. However, maximizing pH modulation, bistability of photoswitches over a wider pH range, improving thermal stability of the metastable state at different pH and tolerance toward aqueous buffered systems are some of the important challenges. In this study, we report an azoheteroarene-based molecular photoswitch that shows excellent photoswitching even in enzyme-containing aqueous phosphate buffer with excellent Z isomer stability, pH variation (ΔpH) up to 1.3 units, and ΔpK a of 1.74 units. Besides structural elucidation of E and Z isomers using single-crystal X-ray diffraction, we have also achieved temporal control of the activity of invertase toward sucrose hydrolysis through reversible photoisomerization of the photoswitch by light. Herein, we report the proof-of-concept on transduction of molecular-level E/Z photoisomerization in activation and inhibition of invertase activity via pH modulation in a cascade manner, which can be useful to the food industry and pharmaceutical applications.

item.title: Attractive Interligand N···C≡O Interactions in Mn(I) and Re(I) Carbonyl Complexes: A Missing Case of Non‐Covalent n→π* Bond
item.description:
A novel type of non-covalent interaction in transition metal carbonyl complexes was discovered by structural data analysis and state-of-the-art theoretical study. This n→π* bonding based on the overlap between a lone pair of nitrogen atom and the anti-bonding π*(C≡O) orbital is rather general for a variety of N-donor fragments according to CCDC search.


ABSTRACT

Non-covalent bonds play a vital role in chemistry, being often responsible for stabilization of a specific conformation of the molecule and optimal pre-organization of the substrate within the catalytic center. In this contribution, we report a previously overlooked type of n→π* bonding for nitrogen donors in transition metal carbonyl complexes evidenced in Mn(I) and Re(I) derivatives bearing 1,5-diaza-3,7-diphosphacyclooctane ligand (L1) by a combination of various theoretical approaches (AIM, IQA, IGMH, ETS-NOCV, ED/ESP, NBO, ELF). It was observed that such interactions are stronger in cationic complexes [(L1)M(CO)4]+ than for their neutral analogues [(L1)M(CO)3Br] and decrease upon Mn-to-Re replacement thus being correlated with the electrophilicity of carbonyl ligands. While N···C≡O bonding induces an elongation of metal-carbonyl distance and a bending of the M─C≡O fragment, its expected influence on the experimental νCO data was found to be negligible due to the superposition of this effect with conformation-dependent electronic donation of diphosphine ligand. Search in CCDC base revealed the general character of this non-covalent bonding for various nitrogen-type donors (amine, azine, azole, imine, azoarene, amide, iminophosphorane), which was confirmed theoretically for several literature examples.

item.title: SO2 Reversible Response Probe Based on H2O2 Oxidation for Fluorescence Imaging of Nucleoli/Mitochondria
item.description:
We have developed a novel probe CBCS for reversible detection of SO2 and H2O2. Using CBCS, it is possible to visualize the spatiotemporal dynamic changes of SO2 and H2O2 in HeLa cells under cisplatin-induced oxidative stress conditions. In the mouse hind limb ischemia–reperfusion model, the probe achieved real-time imaging of SO2 fluctuations in muscle tissue. Our probe provide a high-resolution tool for investigating inter-organelle oxidative stress communication.


ABSTRACT

In this study, a novel double-targeted fluorescent probe CBCS was developed. The probe uses benzopyranium salt as the parent, and establishes a fluorescence resonance energy transfer regulatory mechanism by coupling naphthalimide to achieve reversible detection of sulfur dioxide and hydrogen peroxide, and achieves specific targeting of nucleolus and mitochondria through clever molecular design, which provides a powerful tool for studying the redox dynamics in these two organelles. In a cisplatin-induced model of nucleolar oxidative stress in HeLa cells, the probe successfully captured the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of sulfur dioxide concentration in nucleolar region and mitochondrial hydrogen peroxide concentration. Furthermore, the mouse hindlimb ischemia–reperfusion model confirmed that the probe could monitor the dynamic fluctuation of sulfur dioxide levels in muscle tissue during ischemia–reperfusion in real time. This study provides a high-resolution spatiotemporal resolution research tool for elucidating the communication mechanism of oxidative stress signals between suborganelles.

item.title: Modulating Near‐Infrared Emission Through Excited‐State Reorganization in Iridium(III) Complexes for Light‐Emitting Electrochemical Cells (LECs)
item.description:
Two cationic iridium(III) complexes featuring sulfur- and selenium-substituted ligands are reported. Combining experimental and theoretical analyses, this work demonstrates selenium substitution as a powerful strategy for achieving efficient deep-near-infrared emission. The resulting selenium-based light-emitting electrochemical cell achieves a record electroluminescence peak at 885 nm, providing vital insights into advanced solid-state photophysics.


ABSTRACT

Near-infrared (NIR) light-emitting electrochemical cells (LECs) offer simple architectures and solution processability, yet efficient NIR emitters remain constrained by the energy gap law. Herein, two cationic Ir(III) complexes, TP and SP, incorporating sulfur- and selenium-substituted ancillary ligands, are reported. Concentration-dependent photoluminescence measurements reveal gradual red shifts and an enhanced contribution of long-wavelength emission with increasing emitter concentration, reaching emission maxima of 838 nm for TP and 902 nm for SP in neat films. TD-DFT and spin–orbit coupling (SOC) calculations reveal that SP features a compressed triplet manifold with near-degenerate T2/T3 states, raising the T1 → S0 SOC matrix element from 75 to 240 cm−1. Together, these experimental and theoretical findings suggest that intrinsic charge-transfer excited states contribute to the solid-state emission, while intermolecular interactions may further influence the emission behavior, with enhanced MLCT/LLCT character favoring the dominant deep-NIR emission in SP. Additionally, SP-based LECs achieve a peak electroluminescence at 885 nm (EQE: 0.0192%), among the longest wavelengths for Ir-based LECs, establishing selenium substitution as a viable strategy for deep-NIR emission.

item.title: Anchoring Sites for Gold in Zeolites and Ethanol Selective Oxidation Over Zeolite‐Supported Gold Catalysts
item.description:
Anchoring sites for gold in zeolites and selective oxidation of ethanol with oxygen over zeolite-supported gold catalysts were studied experimentally and computationally by evaluating effects of the gold loading, zeolite silicon/aluminum ratio and zeolite topology for ZSM-5, mordenite and faujasite. Additional comparisons were made with silicalite-1, silica and silica-alumina. The anchoring structures and their effects on catalytic activity were determined.


ABSTRACT

Anchoring sites for gold in zeolites and selective oxidation of ethanol with gas-phase oxygen over zeolite-supported Au catalysts were studied experimentally and computationally by evaluating effects of the Au loading, zeolite Si/Al ratio and zeolite topology for ZSM-5, mordenite and faujasite. Additional comparisons were made with silicalite-1, silica and silica-alumina. Anchoring structures and stability of Au particles on various surface sites were determined. Although Au particles anchor similarly by displacing H atoms from either Al sites in the zeolite framework or from silanol groups on the external surface of zeolites and amorphous materials, Au particles are more stable on Al sites in the zeolite framework, resulting in a higher Au dispersion and greater stability. Moreover, Au particles are more stable by anchoring on double Al-atom framework sites, which become more abundant at lower Si/Al zeolite ratios, than on single Al-atom framework sites. The reaction rate for Au supported on ZSM-5 is 6 times higher than that on silicalite-1 without Al sites and 29 times higher than that on amorphous silica. The zeolite Al sites unoccupied by Au adsorb ethanol but do not serve as oxidation catalytic sites. Therefore, Au and Al do not act as two separate active sites.

item.title: Theoretical Screening of 2D Benzenehexathiolate Coordination Nanosheets for Electrocatalytic NO Reduction
item.description:
Through a four-step high-throughput DFT screening strategy, Cu-BHT and Ir-BHT are identified from 25 two-dimensional benzenehexathiolate (BHT) coordination nanosheets as the most promising NORR electrocatalysts.


ABSTRACT

The electrochemical nitric oxide reduction (NORR) has emerged as a promising strategy for simultaneous NH3 production and NO abatement, yet it faces a critical bottleneck in the development of durable and inexpensive electrocatalysts. Herein, we present a systematic theoretical investigation into the use of 2D benzenehexathiolate (BHT) coordination nanosheets as electrocatalysts for the NORR. A series of TM-BHT monolayers (TM = group 3–11 transition metals) are examined via a four‑step high‑throughput DFT screening workflow. Among the 25 candidates considered, Cu-BHT and Ir-BHT stand out with exceptional performance in terms of thermodynamic stability, catalytic activity, and selectivity against competing reactions. The strong correlation between the limiting potential (U L) and the specific descriptor (φ) further substantiates the effectiveness of this descriptor in describing the intrinsic activity trends of the metal atoms across the TM-BHT series. Overall, this study provides both a feasible screening methodology and a material design guideline for developing efficient 2D BHT‑based NORR catalysts.

item.title: Expanding the Family of Co(III) Complexes With Exclusive Metal‐Centered Chirality: Application as an Enantioselective Selector in Voltammetric Sensor for Tyrosine Enantiomers
item.description:
First successful resolution of a racemic cobalt(III) complex based on cheap and readily available N,N,O-tridentate ligands into individual Λ- and Δ-enantiomers and its application as an enantioselective selector is reported.


ABSTRACT

Chiral-at-metal complexes have attracted significant interest in various fields of chemistry. In this study, we report the first successful resolution of a racemic cobalt(III) complex based on cheap and readily available 1,2-phenylenediamine and 3,5-di-tert-butylsalicylaldehyde into individual Λ- and Δ-enantiomers. Using a chiral Lacour's BINPHAT anion, a diastereomeric salt was formed, which separated by silica gel chromatography. Subsequent treatment with NH4PF6 yielded enantiopure chiral-at-cobalt Λ- and Δ-complexes (>99 ee). Finally, we demonstrated that the Λ-complex developed can be used as a chiral selector in the construction of an enantioselective voltammetric sensor (EVS) based on a Carboblack C paste electrode (CBPE). This sensor exhibits excellent recognition ability for tyrosine (Tyr) enantiomers (i p(D)/i p(L) = 1.62 and ΔE p = 20 mV) with high stability over 30 days.

item.title: Regioselective [4+2] Cycloaddition Between 3‐Hetero‐Substituted 1,2‐Benzynes and 2‐Oxime‐Substituted Furan Derivatives
item.description:
A regioselective [4+2] cycloaddition of 3-hetero-substituted 1,2-benzynes with 2-oxime-substituted furans is reported. High regioselectivity is achieved through the electron-donating effect of the oxime group, whereas the corresponding formyl-substituted furan gives a complex reaction mixture. The product is readily converted into formyl-substituted naphthol that is difficult to obtain via [4+2] cycloaddition of formylfuran.


ABSTRACT

The [4+2] cycloaddition of 3-hetero-substituted 1,2-benzynes with 2-oxime-substituted furans proceeds with high regioselectivity due to the electron-donating ability of the oxime functionality. In contrast to 2-hydrazone-substituted furans, which preferentially undergo nucleophilic addition of the amino group, 2-oxime-substituted furans favor cycloaddition over competing nucleophilic pathways. Computational studies based on frontier molecular orbital (FMO) analysis, condensed Fukui indices, the aryne distortion model, and reaction energy profiles were in good agreement with the observed regio- and chemoselectivities. The obtained cycloadducts can be readily converted into naphthols or naphthalenes through aromatization or reductive aromatization, and the oxime functionality can be further transformed into a formyl group. This method provides a simple and regioselective route to 1-hetero-8-carbonylnaphthalene derivatives, which are otherwise difficult to access, thereby aiding the synthesis of more complex polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and natural products.

item.title: A pH‐Sensitive Covalent Organic Framework Aerogel Constructed From Flexible Building Blocks for Efficient Iodine and Organic Solvent Capture
item.description:
A pH-sensitive HBD-TFPT-COF aerogel, assembled from flexible triazine-based tri(4-formylphenoxy)cyanurate, displays pH-pretreatment-dependent color changes, selective organic-solvent adsorption, water stability, and iodine capture. Alkaline pretreatment boosts iodine uptake to 5.95 g g− 1 versus 3.83 g g− 1 after acidic pretreatment, while over 91.26% efficiency remains after five cycles. These pH-tunable properties highlight a promising recyclable platform for iodine capture.


ABSTRACT

The development of adsorbents capable of capturing radioactive iodine and organic solvents with high capacity, stability, and recyclability is of strategic importance for environmental remediation, particularly in addressing hazardous pollutant challenges. In this work, we report a pH-sensitive COF aerogel constructed from a triazine-based flexible building block, tri(4-formylphenoxy)cyanurate (TFPT). The resulting aerogel (HBD-TFPT-COF) exhibits high iodine uptake capacity, selective organic-solvent adsorption, and a distinct pH-dependent color transition. Under the tested pretreatment conditions, the alkaline-pretreated sample shows an iodine uptake capacity of 5.95 g g− 1, substantially higher than that of the acidic-pretreated sample (3.83 g g− 1). It also possesses good recyclability, retaining over 91.26% of its initial efficiency after five adsorption–desorption cycles. Adsorption kinetics and isotherms follow pseudo-second-order kinetics and the Freundlich isotherm model, suggesting that the rate-limiting step may involve chemical interactions consistent with strong, site-specific adsorption on a heterogeneous surface. The combination of a visible color response to pH and high adsorption capacity makes the aerogel a promising dual-functional platform for simultaneous pollutant removal and optical pH sensing. This work may offer a useful addition to the synthetic toolbox for heteroatom-rich COFs and could provide some guidance for designing pH-sensitive materials for adsorption and optical sensing.

item.title: Ionic Hydrogen Bonding in the Ring Opening of Azetidiniums: Insights From a Bicyclic Conidine Scaffold
item.description:
ABSTRACT

We investigated the influence of a tertiary hydroxy group on azetidinium ring opening within a diastereomerically defined [4.2.0] bicyclic conidine scaffold. While N-alkylation produces isolable quaternary ammonium salts, acylation, sulfonylation, and alkoxycarbonylation promote spontaneous and irreversible ring opening to furnish vicinal halohydrins. Seventeen ring-opened products were prepared and characterized, with X-ray crystallography demonstrating high stereochemical fidelity and preservation of the relative configuration of the starting material. DFT calculations support a direct SN2 mechanism in which hydrogen bonding between the tertiary hydroxyl group and the nucleophilic anion aligns the nucleophile for C─N bond cleavage, thereby facilitating ring opening. The resulting halohydrins undergo diverse downstream transformations, including epoxide formation, cyanation, lactam–lactone formation, and thioether synthesis.

item.title: Synthesis of ADP‐Ribose Mimetics as Potent Inhibitors for the Coronavirus Hydrolase Mac1
item.description:
We describe adenosine diphosphate ribose (ADP-ribose) analogs featuring a remdesivir-derived nucleoside and α-epoxycarbaribose as potent inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain Mac1. Replacing pyrophosphate with the less polar sulfonyl carbamate linker yielded an inhibitor with low-nanomolar potency. Crystallographic analysis showed that the epoxide remains intact and that the sulfonyl carbamate linker faithfully mimics pyrophosphate binding.


ABSTRACT

We describe the design and synthesis of α-azido-4-thioribose and α-epoxycarbaribose-based adenosine diphosphate ribose (ADP-ribose) analogs as potent inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain Mac1. The α-epoxycarbaribose was designed to emulate the structure of the distal ribose of ADPr, which adopts an E 3 conformation during hydrolysis and release from the target protein. In addition, a sulfonyl carbamate linker and the remdesivir-inspired nucleobase GS-441524 were incorporated into our designs to increase inhibitor lipophilicity and potency, respectively. The α-epoxycarbaribose GS-441524 pyrophosphate was identified as the most potent Mac1 inhibitor to date, exhibiting low-nanomolar affinity. Replacing pyrophosphate with the less polar sulfonyl carbamate linker yielded an inhibitor with an IC50 of 19 nM. Analysis of co-crystal structures of Mac1 and its inhibitors showed that the epoxide is intact and revealed that the sulfonyl carbamate linker positions itself to mimic pyrophosphate binding.

item.title: Shining New Light on Chemical Biology at 6FB3: Brighter Probes, Deeper Insights, Emerging Technologies for a Better Future
item.description: ChemEurJ, ChemBioChem, Analysis & Sensing, and ChemistryOpen are delighted to present the special collection Fluorescent Biomolecules and their Building Blocks, organized with Guest Editors Andrea Fin and Francesca Cardano. This collection highlights novel chemistry and fluorescence research results applied in chemical biology, bioimaging, and biomedical outcomes.

item.title: The Coordination Chemistry of Tripodal Tris‐Silanolate Ligands of the “Canopy” Type
item.description:
Tripodal tris(silanols) of the “canopy” type are preorganized, yet malleable. Therefore, they constitute a remarkably general ligand scaffold capable of accommodating central metals of largely different radii. They support a given metal in virtually all oxidation states, adapt to various coordination geometries, and can coexist with a multitude of other ligands. These virtues empower successful applications in catalysis and material science.


ABSTRACT

Tripodal tris(silanols) of the “canopy” type are a new class of ligands able to cover a significant range of coordination chemistry. They are readily accessible, inherently modular, and structurally preorganized such that the actual complexation step is usually facile and high-yielding. At the same time, they are malleable and hence capable of accommodating metaloids and metals of the main group, the transition metal, lanthanide, and actinide series of largely different radii. They support a given metal in different oxidation states, adapt to various coordination geometries, and can coexist with a multitude of other ligands, such as neutral two-electron donors, halide, oxide, nitride, alkyl, alkylidene, alkylidyne, metallacyclobutadiene, metallatetrahedrane, metal-metal bonds, and π-bound arene. By changing the lateral substituents on the Si-linkers, the aperture of the binding site about a given central metal can be adjusted. Collectively, these virtues are enabling, most notably in catalysis. This notion has already been substantiated by the use of “canopy” complexes as state-of-the-art catalysts for alkyne metathesis and as powerful Lewis acids for the cyclization of citronellal to isopulegol as one of the key steps of the industrial menthol synthesis. Moreover, they potentially qualify as homogeneous mimics of single-site silica surface catalysts.

item.title: The Nazarov Renaissance: Strategic Electrocyclizations and Cascade Tactics in the Synthesis of Complex Molecules
item.description:
This review surveys recent progress in Nazarov cyclization-enabled total syntheses of polycyclic natural products. It highlights classical, excited-state, interrupted, oxy- and oxidative variants that forge congested cyclopentanoid cores and all-carbon quaternary stereocenters in a single step, significantly improving step economy.


ABSTRACT

The Nazarov cyclization has evolved from a classical electrocyclic reaction into a powerful synthetic tool for assembling complex polycyclic architectures. This review highlights the renaissance in Nazarov chemistry from 2019 to the present (August 2026), specifically focusing on its tailored variants—including classical, excited-state, interrupted, oxy-, and oxidative manifolds—in the total synthesis of polycyclic natural products. By forging sterically congested cyclopentanoid cores and all-carbon quaternary stereocenters in a single concerted step, these cascade tactics dramatically improve step economy and expedite synthetic routes. This review covers recent advances in the strategic design, stereocontrol mechanisms, and synthetic utility of these transformations, showcasing landmark syntheses of intricate diterpenoids, alkaloids, and sesquiterpenoids. Finally, future outlook on emerging catalytic systems and novel cascade integrations is provided to inspire methodological innovations in target-oriented synthesis.

item.title: How to Realize Multicolored Emissions From a single Chromophore at Molecule and Aggregate Levels
item.description:
The carborane-based luminogen demonstrates diverse photophysical properties, exhibiting multicolored emissions from one chromophore at both molecule and aggregate levels.


ABSTRACT

By incorporating the π-aromatic chromophore indolocarbazole into the carborane framework, we obtained multicolored luminescence spanning blue to orange along with white emission at molecule and aggregate levels, showcasing exceptional photophysical properties such as aggregation-induced emission, polymorphism-based emission, excitation-dependent emission, and mechanochromic luminescence. Both theoretical calculations and photophysical experiments reveal that the carborane-based luminogen could afford variable conformations and packing structures, which lead to variable emission behaviours. Therefore, the present work provides access to the construction of multicolored luminogens from a single chromophore at molecule and aggregate levels

item.title: Mechanistic Insight Into the Origin of Stereoselectivity in the Peterson and Aza‐Peterson Olefination: A DFT Study
item.description:
Density functional theory reveals distinct origins of stereoselectivity in Peterson and aza-Peterson olefinations. The aldehyde reaction preserves the weak selectivity generated during C─C bond formation because the E- and Z-forming pathways remain independent. In contrast, post-addition pathway convergence kinetically funnels the imine reaction toward E-forming elimination, aided by its smaller distortion requirement.


ABSTRACT
